clue.text: A means to access the subconscious is a constitutional right

definitions.text: A means to access the subconscious
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the psychoanalytic technique of saying whatever comes to mind
second meaning: the liberty to associate freely with others, protected under the US First Amendment

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one claim linking therapy and law; it is two separate senses of the same phrase joined by 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's technique of unprompted word linking shares its name with the civil liberty of joining groups without interference.

clue.text: Stiff, intoxicated nights after initial slugfests

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger out of order, so these are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: what comes after the initial of nights is the word minus its first letter

parts.note: taken as written, before losing its first letter

explanation.surface: Drunken nights after early brawls leave someone stiff and sore.
explanation.definitionFit: A slugfest is a bout of heavy punching, and a fistfight is a brawl with bare hands.

clue.text: In the end, inventive segment by colony member is tasteful

indicators.note: the end of the word inventive is its final letter

parts.note: taken as written; only its last letter is used
a leg is a stage or segment of a journey
ants live in colonies

explanation.surface: An art review praising a creative section by a member of an artists' colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colony member' invites thoughts of settlers or artists; here it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and refined in style, the quality that good taste produces.

clue.text: God recalling prince to Western city

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V
LA is Los Angeles, in the American West

explanation.surface: A deity reminisces about a prince who travelled to a city in the West.
explanation.definitionFit: Allah is the Arabic word for God, used by Muslims and Arabic-speaking Christians alike.

clue.text: Lease condominium in part, usually the lower part

indicators.note: only part of these two words is used, the letters that span the gap between them

parts.note: taken as written; the answer runs across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A rental contract covers part of a condo, typically the downstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like the lower floor of a building, but it is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: In a piano duet the secondo is the second player's part, normally the bass end of the keyboard.

clue.text: 151–100 — he's wiped the floor with, made mincemeat of, and so forth

definitions.text: wiped the floor with, made mincemeat of, and so forth

parts.note: CLI is 151 in Roman numerals
C is the Roman numeral for 100
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A sports report of a lopsided 151 to 100 win, piling on stock phrases about the victor.
explanation.walkthrough: The score reads as a dash between numbers, but each number simply becomes its Roman numeral in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrases listed are tired, overused expressions for beating someone, examples of hackneyed stock phrases.

clue.text: Hawk and I practice, irregularly

indicators.note: the letters are set out in an irregular order

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A falconer admits that he and his bird train only now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Accipiter is the genus of short-winged hawks, such as the goshawk and sparrowhawk.

clue.text: I sent no Baroque chants

indicators.note: baroque means ornate and convoluted, so the letters are twisted into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A choir director confesses to never having sent out any Baroque plainsong.
explanation.walkthrough: Baroque looks like the musical period, which suits the singing; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to recite or sing in a steady monotone, the way liturgical chant is delivered.

clue.text: Northeast street is home for some

explanation.surface: A street in the northeast of town is where some people live.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is the dwelling built by birds and some insects, so it is a home for certain creatures.

clue.text: Outside, he hollers back for coat

indicators.note: the reversed shouts sit outside the word he, wrapping around it
the word for hollers is read in the backward direction

parts.note: to holler is to call out
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone standing outdoors yells for their jacket to be brought out to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin varnish used as a protective finish, and to shellac a surface is to coat it.

clue.text: Arouses one ugly insect

indicators.note: an ugly version of something is a distorted one, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A single unsightly bug provokes a reaction, perhaps disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to stir up or provoke feelings or action, the same as to arouse them.

clue.text: Gordon captured by sweeping camera shot — his performance is disappointing

parts.note: Flash Gordon is the comic-strip space hero
something captured by a shot is in it
a pan is a horizontal sweep of the camera, hence the pan

explanation.surface: A film critic notes that the actor playing Gordon, caught in a panning shot, gives a weak performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a person, which the idiom can mean: someone whose early promise came to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from old muskets whose priming powder flared without firing: a showy start that delivers nothing.

clue.text: Subversive, low reds, conniving in silence

indicators.note: subversion overturns order, so the letters are overturned too

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
a conniving person is sly

explanation.surface: Undercover communists plot quietly against the state.
explanation.walkthrough: Low reds reads as lowly communists, fitting subversive; the phrase is only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without speaking a word is doing it silently.

clue.text: Communicate with cooked escargots

indicators.note: cooked suggests something altered or fiddled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A diner tries to make conversation over a plate of snails.
explanation.definitionFit: To get an idea across is to make it understood, which is what communicating it achieves.

clue.text: Hooker entering backwards (etc.) in Southern city

indicators.note: the prostitute goes inside the reversed letters
the abbreviation etc is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
a hooker is a prostitute, a harlot

explanation.surface: A news snippet about a Civil War general named Hooker marching into a Southern town.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Hooker was a Union general, which makes the surface feel historical.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte is the largest city in North Carolina, in the American South.

clue.text: Renaissance poet to bring donkey inside

indicators.note: together with inside, this tells us to place one piece within another
the donkey is put inside the little word to

parts.note: taken as written
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: Instructions to a Renaissance poet to lead his donkey indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was the sixteenth-century Italian author of the epic Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: Portia rarely sports a headband

indicators.note: to sport is to wear or display, and the first two words wear the answer within them

parts.note: taken as written; the answer straddles the two words

explanation.surface: A woman called Portia seldom wears a hairband.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head, a decorative form of headband.

clue.text: Eccentric red coat, in a style from the 1920s

indicators.note: something eccentric is off-centre and odd, so the letters are set oddly

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An unusual scarlet jacket cut in a Jazz Age fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the geometric design movement that flourished in the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: For example, spider or honeybee's head stuck in broken trapdoor

indicators.note: the single letter is lodged inside the rearranged letters
a broken trapdoor has its letters smashed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written; only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A spider or a bee's head is caught in a broken trapdoor, as in a gruesome nature scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Trapdoor spiders exist, which makes the surface plausible; the honeybee contributes only its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiders belong to the arthropods, the jointed-limbed invertebrate phylum that also includes insects and crustaceans.

clue.text: Pavement brings snake to a stop

parts.note: the asp is a venomous snake
coming to a halt is coming to a stop

explanation.surface: A road surface makes a slithering serpent freeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is the tarry mixture used to surface roads, so it is paving material.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory report includes zero for soldier

indicators.note: the rearranged report holds the zero within it
an unsatisfactory report is a poor one, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A poor school report with a zero on it is handed to a young soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a private soldier, originally in a cavalry or armoured unit.

clue.text: Harrow or a plow in act affecting the needy

indicators.note: to harrow is to break up soil, so the letters are broken up and reset

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A farm question, harrow or plow, set beside legislation for the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow sits naturally beside plow as farm gear; here it is a verb telling us to churn the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The English Poor Laws were statutes for relief of paupers, legislation governing aid to the destitute.

clue.text: Part of the infrastructure to call John Paul II, for instance

parts.note: to telephone someone is to call them
Pope John Paul II was Polish, so he is an example of a Pole

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what to name the late pontiff as part of some grand structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Utility poles carrying phone lines are a basic piece of the physical network serving a community.

clue.text: Grant termination that hurts

parts.note: an end is a termination
ow is what someone says when something hurts

explanation.surface: A painful cut-off of someone's funding grant.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give money or property, especially a permanent fund to an institution.

clue.text: Bowling equipment cut up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to snip is to cut

explanation.surface: Gear in a bowling alley gets slashed by vandals.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten-pin bowlers aim at pins, the wooden targets knocked down by the ball.

clue.text: I retain irrational resistance to change

indicators.note: an irrational ordering is a senseless one, so the letters are shuffled out of sense

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to an unreasonable stubbornness about new things.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is the tendency of a body or person to stay as it is unless pushed, a reluctance to alter.

clue.text: Hawks bicycles on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so a word that sounds the same will do

parts.note: to bicycle is to pedal

explanation.surface: A news item about birds of prey and bikes heard over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To hawk goods is to sell them by going about offering them, exactly what a pedlar does.

clue.text: Oliver's trash is nearby

parts.note: film director Oliver Stone, so belonging to Stone
to trash something is to throw it away

explanation.surface: A remark that the director's rubbish is lying around close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something a short throw of a pebble away is close by, so the idiom means within easy reach.
